parts.latex:
Chelsea collected data on the teacher bullying rate and the age of students at the college. The results were graphed and a line of best fit was drawn by four different students as shown.

7726.stem:
After a class of ten students sits a test on Monday, the teacher spends time doing revision and tests the students again on Friday. Only nine of the students are present for the second test on Friday. The results, in percentages, for those nine students, are shown in the following table.

\extable{3297_q20_t1}

figures.cap: scatter plot of Friday against Monday test results with line y = x
solution sketch: scatter plot with H and I added

parts.latex:
Add the results of students H and I to the scatter plot.

\exfigure{3297_q20_1}

The equation of least-squares line of best fit is given by $y = mx + c$ where

$$m = r\dfrac{S_y}{S_x} \text{ and } c = \bar{y} - m\bar{x}$$

Using these formulas or otherwise, determine the equation of the least-squares line of best fit. Answer correct to 2 decimal places.
Using your answer to part (b), predict the result for the student who was absent for Friday’s test. Give your answer to the nearest whole mark.
The scatterplot above also shows the line $y = x$. Explain the significance of a student being represented below the line $y = x$.

solutions.latex: \exfigure{3297_q20_s1}

From the statistics of the data:
$$\begin{aligned} r &= 0.6602\ldots & s_x &= 5.28625\ldots & s_y &= 4.99444\ldots \\ \bar{x} &= 56.7777\ldots & \bar{y} &= 59.2222\ldots \end{aligned}$$
Gradient:
$$\begin{aligned} m &= r\dfrac{s_y}{s_x} \\ &= 0.6602\ldots \times \dfrac{4.99444\ldots}{5.28625\ldots} \\ &= 0.62375\ldots \end{aligned}$$
Intercept:
$$\begin{aligned} c &= \bar{y} - m\bar{x} \\ &= 59.2222\ldots - 0.62375\ldots \times 56.7777\ldots \\ &= 23.8066\ldots \end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore\ y = 0.62x + 23.81$$
criteria: Gets gradient and $y$-intercept correct, but does not provide equation of line, or equivalent merit
Gets either gradient or $y$-intercept correct, not both, or equivalent merit

solutions.latex:
Substitute $x = 63$ into the line from part (b):
$$\begin{aligned} y &= 0.62 \times 63 + 23.81 \\ &= 62.87 \\ &\approx 63 \end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore\ \text{predicted result} = 63 \text{ (to the nearest whole mark)}$$
criteria: Uses equation from (b) to find correct answer

solutions.latex: A student who appears below the line $y = x$ performed better on Monday’s test.

parts.latex: What is Pearson's correlation coefficient? Answer correct to 4 decimal places.
Find the equation of the least-squares line of best fit in terms of years ($t$) and height ($h$). Answer correct to 2 decimal places.
Hayden did not record the tree's height after five years. Predict the height after five years, correct to one decimal place.
Use algebra to estimate how many years it will take for the tree to reach a height of 20 metres. Answer correct to 1 decimal place.
Comment on the reliability of your answers in (c) and (d).

solutions.latex:
Using the calculator,
$$\begin{aligned} r &= 0.99519\ldots \\ &\approx 0.9952 \end{aligned}$$
This shows strong positive correlation.

The line has the form $y = mx + c$; the calculator gives $y = Bx + A$, so
$$H = 1.19t - 0.85$$
Alternatively, use the approximate line of best fit through $(4, 4)$ and $(9, 10)$:
$$\begin{aligned} m &= \dfrac{y_2 - y_1}{x_2 - x_1} \\ &= \dfrac{10 - 4}{9 - 4} \\ &= \dfrac{6}{5} \\ &= 1.2 \end{aligned}$$
\exfigure{708_q20_s1}
criteria: Finds the gradient or intercept correctly, or equivalent merit
Attempts to use the calculator or two points on the line, or equivalent merit

meta.marker_note: Students could use rise/run for $m$; the marker judges whether the points chosen on the line of best fit are appropriate and marks using the student's value of $m$.
meta.format_note: Source had only a marker note as criterion; rubric written by us from the 3 marks.

solutions.latex:
Substitute $t = 5$ into the line of best fit.
$$\begin{aligned} H &= 1.19 \times 5 - 0.85 \\ &\approx 5.1\text{ m} \end{aligned}$$

Substitute $H = 20$ into the line of best fit and solve for $t$.
$$\begin{aligned} 20 &= 1.19t - 0.85 \\ 20.85 &= 1.19t \\ t &= 17.5\text{ years} \end{aligned}$$
criteria: Substitutes $H = 20$ and rearranges correctly, or equivalent merit

meta.format_note: Source criterion 'logical worked solution and answer' rewritten top-down.

solutions.latex:
There is a strong positive linear association.

Part (c) involves interpolation (within the data), which is very reliable.

Part (d) involves extrapolation (beyond the data), which is less reliable.
criteria: Comments on one of interpolation or extrapolation, or equivalent merit

7833.stem:
Some students had their heights and head circumferences measured in centimetres, and recorded in the table below.

\extable{2841_q2c_t1}

parts.latex: Find $r$ for this set of data, correct to 3 decimal places, and describe the strength of association between the two variables.
Complete the table above with the mean and standard deviation of the students' head circumferences. Round the standard deviation to 4 decimal places.

Using the formulas below, find the equation of least squares line of best fit, correct to 4 significant figures.

$$m = r \times \dfrac{s_y}{s_x} \qquad \text{and} \qquad c = \bar{y} - m\bar{x}$$
Using the equation found in part (iii), predict the head circumference of a student who is 190 cm tall, to the nearest centimetre.
Using the equation found in part (iii), predict how tall a student would be who has a head circumference of 49 cm, to the nearest centimetre.
What is the meaning of the gradient of the line found in part (iii) in this context?

solutions.latex:
$$r = 0.797$$
Strong positive correlation.

meta.format_note: Rubric was two separate 1-mark rows (correct r; strong positive); rewritten top-down.

solutions.latex: $$\text{Mean} = 50.75,\quad \text{standard deviation} = 1.7139$$

Using $m = r\times\dfrac{s_y}{s_x}$,
$$\begin{aligned} m &= 0.797\times\dfrac{1.7139}{11.9452} \\ &= 0.1144 \end{aligned}$$
Using $c = \bar{y} - m\bar{x}$,
$$\begin{aligned} c &= 50.75 - 0.1144\times 174.25 \\ &= 30.82 \end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore\ y = 0.1144x + 30.82$$
criteria: Correct gradient or intercept, or equivalent merit

meta.format_note: Source had no criteria; rubric written by us (2 marks per question).

solutions.latex:
Substitute $x = 190$ into the line.
$$\begin{aligned} y &= 0.1144\times 190 + 30.82 \\ &= 52.5511\ldots \\ &\approx 53 \text{ cm} \end{aligned}$$

Substitute $y = 49$ into the line.
$$\begin{aligned} 49 &= 0.1144x + 30.82 \\ 0.1144x &= 18.18 \\ x &= \dfrac{18.18}{0.1144} \\ &= 158.9\ldots \\ &\approx 159 \text{ cm} \end{aligned}$$
The gradient is $0.1144$, so for each centimetre taller, the head circumference increases by $0.1144$ cm.

The points trend downward, so the gradient is negative. This rules out C and D.

Test the remaining lines at the ends of the data.

Option A: $y=130-3.8x$ gives $y=130-190=-60$ at $x=50$, but the data there are about $30$ to $65$, so it fails.

Option B: $y=145-1.7x$ gives $y=145-17=128$ at $x=10$, $y=145-51=94$ at $x=30$ and $y=145-85=60$ at $x=50$. These fit the centre of the data.

Hence the answer is option B.

meta.self_check: Evaluated candidate lines at x=10,30,50 against scatterplot.

The light grid is every 2 in x and every 10 in y, with darker lines every 10 in x and every 50 in y. Axes have -latex arrows (rule 4) and there is an open circle at the origin. The remaining colour in the overlay is the faint grey grid and the tick-label font. Rules 1–4, 4a, 11 and 19 applied.

7940.stem:
The cost of catering is related to the number of people attending an event, as per the table below.

\extable{3295_q6a_t1}

parts.latex: Find the Pearson's correlation coefficient ($r$) correct to 4 decimal places.
Describe the relationship between the number of people at an event and the cost.
Calculate the mean and sample standard deviation of the number of people, $\bar{x}$ and $S_x$. Give your answer correct to 2 decimal places.
parts.note: Asks for the sample standard deviation S_x; only population sigma is in the 2024 course.

parts.latex: Calculate the mean and sample standard deviation of the cost, $\bar{y}$ and $S_y$. Give your answer correct to 2 decimal places.
parts.note: Asks for the sample standard deviation S_y; only population sigma is in the 2024 course.

parts.latex:
The equation of the least-squares regression line is given by:

$$y = mx + c$$

where the gradient (or slope) is $m = r\dfrac{S_y}{S_x}$.

and y-intercept is $c = \bar{y} - m\bar{x}$.

Using these equations, show that the equation of the least-squares regression line is

$$y = 3.57x + 51.83.$$
Use the equation to calculate the cost of catering for one hundred people.

solutions.latex: Strong and positive relationship.

criteria: Correct mean or correct standard deviation, or equivalent merit
Correct mean or correct standard deviation, or equivalent merit

solutions.latex:
Substitute into the given formulas.
$$\begin{aligned} m &= r\dfrac{S_y}{S_x} \\ &= 0.9946 \times \dfrac{54.35}{15.14} \\ &\approx 3.57 \end{aligned}$$
$$\begin{aligned} c &= \bar{y} - m\bar{x} \\ &= 150 - 3.57(27.5) \\ &\approx 51.83 \end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore\ y = 3.57x + 51.83$$
criteria: Shows the correct value of $m$ or $c$, or equivalent merit

solutions.latex:
Substitute $x = 100$.
$$\begin{aligned} y &= 3.57 \times 100 + 51.83 \\ &= \$408.83 \end{aligned}$$
